## Eight common assumptions, negated

| # | Usual assumption | If it were false, what conditional effect follows |
|---|---|---|
| A1 | L2 strength (alpha) acts the same at every batch size. | sklearn-style L2 is scaled by 1/batch_size and applied once per step. Small batches then compound the penalty, so raising alpha hurts more at batch 4–10. Large batches have little gradient noise, so L2 becomes the only regularizer and raising alpha helps more there. |
| A2 | Under Adam, width can be scaled without retuning the learning rate. | Under standard parameterization, the effective step grows with width. Widening then hurts at high learning rates and helps at low ones, where extra capacity makes up for undertraining. |
| A3 | Depth is roughly neutral on tabular data. | Depth interacts with optimization and regularization. Adding a layer hurts under strong alpha or a low learning rate and helps when the learning rate is in its good range. |
| A4 | The cost of alpha does not depend on how many parameters it covers. | The penalty sums over all layers and units. Deep or wide nets are over-regularized first, so raising alpha hurts more there. |
| A5 | Batch noise and alpha are separate dials. | They substitute for each other. Shrinking the batch helps most when alpha is low and hurts most when alpha is high (double regularization). |
| A6 | Increasing batch size is harmless with a fixed epoch budget. | It cuts the number of update steps. That hurts most when the learning rate is low or the net is large and needs both noise and steps. |
| A7 | Learning-rate tolerance does not depend on architecture. | Wide or deep nets have sharper curvature, while shallow nets tolerate large steps. Large batches justify larger learning rates (linear-scaling logic). |
| A8 | Width and depth are interchangeable sources of capacity. | A one-layer net relies entirely on width, and a narrow layer bottlenecks added depth. Cutting width therefore hurts more at depth 1, and adding depth hurts more at low width. |

- Used twice: batch_size low/high, learning_rate_init low/high, depth low/high, alpha high, width low/high.
- Used once: alpha low and learning_rate_init mid.
